vv.description: VS Code host shell for Verilog visualization and a digital-circuit sandbox (digitaljs simulation)
vv.untrusted: This extension starts no child processes and runs no executables from the workspace: Yosys/DigitalJS are WASM bundled with the extension; workspace content is only read as text and rendered as a diagram. Without this declaration the host would not activate the extension in a never-trusted folder (symptom: a Welcome (Restricted Mode) page only, no error, nothing in the log).
vv.cmd.verilogVisualizer.revealProjectDi: Open Containing Folder (to verify on disk)
vv.config.verilogViz.compile.topModule: Top module name for compilation. Leave empty to use the first module defined in the entry file.
vv.config.verilogViz.compile.noFlatten: Don't flatten the hierarchy (keep module boundaries).
vv.config.verilogViz.compile.noOpt: Don't optimize (keep the original gate structure).
vv.config.verilogViz.compile.autoRecompi: Recompile and refresh the canvas when a `.v` file is saved (while the canvas panel is open).
vv.config.verilogViz.sandbox.showGrid: Show the grid on the sandbox canvas.
vv.config.verilogViz.sandbox.snapToGrid: Snap parts to the grid while dragging.
vv.config.verilogViz.sandbox.defaultBits: Default bit width for new IO parts.
vv.config.verilogViz.sandbox.autoStartSi: Start the simulation automatically when opening a sandbox.
vv.config.verilogViz.sandbox.foldConstan: In read-only views, fold "operator + constant input" into a circle.
vv.config.verilogViz.bindings.policy: Fallback policy for expanding subpart instances on the sandbox canvas (R152 ruling: **compilation is always binding-authoritative** — unrecorded instances never fall back by name and fail with a hint to "write complete bindings"; this setting only affects the canvas): **auto** = unrecorded subcircuit instances expand via same-name parts, with a visible "write them all" hint; **strict** = no fallback on the canvas either — unrecorded subpart instances stay collapsed until "Write Complete Binding Config" fills them in.
